prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” service that guarantees whether large language models will recommend your business, because different AI systems use different data sources and update at different times. The practical best approach is to (1) make sure your business is listed and authoritative in the sources those AIs draw from, and (2) monitor those sources with one or two dedicated tools.

Recommended combination (what most businesses use)
- Google Business Profile (free): absolutely essential. AIs often draw on Google Maps / Knowledge Panel info. Keep it complete and verified.
- Yext (listings + AI/knowledge-graph features): enterprise-grade for distributing authoritative listings to many publishers and optimizing for knowledge-graph/AI visibility. Good if you want a single control point and paid solution that advertises generative-AI readiness.
- BrightLocal or Moz Local (local SEO monitoring): affordable for small businesses. They track local rankings, citations, and reviews (how you appear in Maps, Yelp, etc.).
- Reputation.com / Synup / Uberall: alternatives that focus on listings + review management at scale.

Why this combo works
- Generative AIs often synthesize info from trusted sources such as Google Maps/Knowledge Panel, Yelp, TripAdvisor, Wikipedia/Wikidata, major directories, news, and authoritative sites. If your info is inconsistent or missing in those places, the AI is less likely to surface you.
- Tools above help (a) get correct, consistent NAP (name/address/phone) across directories, (b) push rich metadata (hours, menu, services, images), (c) gather reviews, and (d) monitor how you appear in local search.

How to test whether an AI recommends you
1. Query multiple models:
   - ChatGPT (use the web/browsing-enabled version or plug-ins if available)
   - Bing Chat (uses live web results)
   - Google Bard
   - Apple Siri / Alexa (voice assistants)
2. Use realistic prompts. Examples:
   - “Recommend the best coffee shops near [neighborhood, city].”
   - “I’m visiting [city] and want [service]. List top local businesses and why.”
   - “Show the phone and address for the best [business type] in [city].”
3. Ask for citations or sources: “Cite where you got that info” — models with browsing or citations will show the origin.
4. Repeat over time and after you update listings — generative engines can change quickly.

Practical next steps (if you want an action plan)
- Claim and optimize Google Business Profile (photos, services, hours, posts).
- Ensure accurate listings on Yelp, Apple Maps, TripAdvisor (if relevant), Facebook, and key local directories.
- Add structured data (schema.org) to your website (LocalBusiness, Product, Service, Reviews).
- Build a short Wikipedia/Wikidata entry if the business meets notability (or get authoritative mentions in local news/blogs).
- Use BrightLocal or Moz Local to audit and monitor citations and rankings monthly.
- Use Yext or Synup if you prefer a single paid platform to push updates everywhere.

If you want, tell me your business name + city and I’ll:
- Check publicly visible listings and major directories,
- Give a short assessment of where you’re missing or inconsistent,
- Suggest which monitoring/management tool fits your budget.
